title: Microsoft Purview: bulk replacement or removal of retention labels (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the briefing says changing or removing a label changes how long an item is kept or when it is deleted, without accounting for other retention settings or labels that enforce no actions. Microsoft documents both exceptions. The roadmap details and the existing role-management path and command are supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Retention labels provide item-level retention and deletion settings.
claims.quote: A retention label (however it was applied) provides explicit retention in comparison with retention policies, because the retention settings are applied to an individual item rather than implicitly assigned from a container.

claims.claim: Replacing or removing a retention label changes how long that item is kept or when it is deleted.
claims.quote: These two actions are calculated independently from each other, from all the retention settings applied to an item. ... you can also use retention labels without turning on any retention or other actions.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Replacing or removing a retention label can change the item's retention or deletion outcome, depending on the label's actions and other retention settings applied to the item.' Retain the citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: An auto-apply retention label policy never replaces an existing label applied to content.
claims.quote: An auto-apply retention label policy will never replace an existing retention label that's applied to content.

claims.claim: The documented end-of-retention relabelling methods cannot change a label that marks items as regulatory records.
claims.quote: You can't use these relabeling methods if the existing label is configured to mark items as a regulatory record.
